title: 🔍 Similarity Criteria — AA, SSS, SAS
hook: Have you ever enlarged a photo? The bigger photo has the same shape but different size — every angle is the same, and all dimensions are scaled by the same factor. That's similarity in geometry!
explanation:
Similar Triangles: Two triangles are similar if their corresponding angles are equal AND corresponding sides are proportional. Written: △ABC ~ △DEF.

Three ways to prove triangles are similar:

CriterionWhat you needExample
AA (Angle-Angle)Two pairs of equal angles∠A = ∠D and ∠B = ∠E → △ABC ~ △DEF
SSS (Side-Side-Side)All three side ratios equalAB/DE = BC/EF = CA/FD
SAS (Side-Angle-Side)One equal angle between proportional sides∠A = ∠D and AB/DE = AC/DF
If △ABC ~ △DEF, then: AB/DE = BC/EF = CA/FD (corresponding sides in the SAME order!).
⚠️ Tip: The ORDER matters! △ABC ~ △DEF means A↔D, B↔E, C↔F. Write them in the correct correspondence!
worked_example:
Example: In △ABC and △PQR: ∠A = 50°, ∠B = 70°, ∠P = 50°, ∠R = 60°. Are they similar?

1
Find missing angles
∠C = 180° − 50° − 70° = 60°. ∠Q = 180° − 50° − 60° = 70°.
2
Compare angles
∠A = ∠P = 50°, ∠B = ∠Q = 70°, ∠C = ∠R = 60°
3
By AA criterion
△ABC ~ △PQR (all angles match in this order)

try_this.question: △ABC has AB = 4, BC = 6, CA = 8. △DEF has DE = 2, EF = 3, FD = 4. Are they similar?
try_this.hint: Check if all side ratios are equal: AB/DE, BC/EF, CA/FD.
try_this.answer: AB/DE = 4/2 = 2, BC/EF = 6/3 = 2, CA/FD = 8/4 = 2. All ratios equal → △ABC ~ △DEF by SSS.

fun_fact: Similarity is the basis of map-making! Every map is a 'similar figure' to the actual land — same shape, different scale.
